title: eslint-rspack-plugin 5.0.0 Ships as a Pure ESM Package, Aligning with the Rstack Ecosystem
gist: eslint-rspack-plugin 5.0.0 drops its CommonJS build to become a pure ESM package, following Rspack 2.0's own ESM-only pivot. The more interesting signal is that the project's own README and the Rsbuild FAQ both advise against using the plugin at all — and the Rstack team now ships Rslint, a Go-based ESLint-compatible linter it claims is 20-40x faster, pointing to linting moving out of the bundler entirely.

themes.theme: Pure ESM as an ecosystem-wide forcing function

insights.claim: eslint-rspack-plugin 5.0.0 removed its CommonJS build and now publishes only as pure ESM, mirroring Rspack 2.0's republishing of its core packages as ESM-only.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A major bundler ecosystem is now dropping CJS at the core-package level, not just adding ESM alongside it — a migration marker for anyone maintaining JS toolchain dependencies.
insights.quote: The move mirrors Rspack 2.0, which republished its core packages as pure ESM and dropped their CommonJS builds to make module loading more consistent and better aligned with current Node.js practices.

insights.claim: The practical blast radius of the ESM-only break is small because Node.js 20 and later can load ESM modules via require(esm), so most projects consuming the plugin through the JavaScript API need no code changes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: require(esm) in Node 20+ is what makes CJS-dropping safe for maintainers — expect the rest of the JS tooling ecosystem to use the same justification.
insights.quote: Because Node.js 20 and later can already load ESM modules using require(esm), most projects consuming the plugin through the JavaScript API should see little practical impact and need no code changes.

insights.claim: A major version number here signals packaging policy rather than functionality: the plugin's behaviour, options surface and watch-mode incremental linting carry forward unchanged from the 4.x line.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Semver majors in the JS toolchain increasingly encode module-format decisions, so read them as distribution changes before assuming feature churn.
insights.locator: Functionally the plugin continues to run ESLint

themes.theme: A tool that recommends against itself

insights.claim: The eslint-rspack-plugin README explicitly advises developers that they may find it more efficient to avoid the plugin entirely, because running ESLint during the build lengthens build times, and recommends a separate lint command instead.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: When maintainers document their own tool as the slower path, treat build-integrated linting as a legacy pattern rather than a default.
insights.quote: you may find it more efficient to avoid using the eslint-rspack-plugin, as running ESLint during the build can lead to longer build times,

insights.claim: Rsbuild does not run ESLint during builds by default, stating the reason as protecting compilation performance, and @rsbuild/plugin-eslint repeats the same warning despite wrapping the plugin internally.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The default configuration of the framework already encodes the anti-pattern verdict — opting in is a deliberate performance trade.

insights.claim: Caching is enabled by default in the 5.x option set specifically to reduce execution time, an admission that lint-in-build cost is significant enough to require mitigation out of the box.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Defaults reveal where the pain is: caching-on-by-default plus a thread-pool option means linting cost is the plugin's defining constraint.

insights.claim: The Rstack team now ships Rslint, a TypeScript-first, ESLint-compatible linter written in Go and powered by typescript-go, which it claims delivers 20 to 40 times faster linting than traditional ESLint setups.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: A 20-40x claim with ESLint compatibility is the kind of margin that flips defaults within a release cycle; watch ESLint's position in the JS toolchain.
insights.quote: which it claims delivers 20 to 40 times faster linting than traditional ESLint setups
insights.locator: The Rstack team now ships Rslint

insights.claim: The direction of travel is that a fast standalone linter — ESLint via a dedicated script, or an alternative such as Rslint — increasingly beats linting inside the bundler, meaning bundler-integrated lint plugins are a shrinking category.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Architectural signal: linting is decoupling from bundling, which changes where CI time is spent and which vendors capture it.
insights.quote: For teams chasing build speed, running a fast standalone linter, whether ESLint through a dedicated script or an alternative such as Rslint, increasingly looks preferable to linting inside the bundler itself.
insights.locator: That caveat reflects a broader shift

insights.claim: The same organisation maintains both the ESLint-in-bundler plugin and the Go-based replacement that undercuts it, so Rstack is effectively funding the deprecation of its own integration path.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Maintenance risk for anyone standardising on the plugin — the incumbent's own roadmap points elsewhere.
insights.locator: That caveat reflects a broader shift

insights.claim: Upgraders from 4.x are advised to test the pure ESM change against their toolchain and, where practical, adopt ESLint's flat config via configType: 'flat', indicating flat config is now the recommended default rather than an option.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: The eslintrc-to-flat-config migration is being pulled forward by bundler upgrades — bundle the two migrations rather than sequencing them.

insights.claim: The lintAllFiles option exists because multi-environment Rsbuild and Rspack builds run separate client and server passes that would otherwise skip files outside each pass's dependency graph, silently leaving code unlinted.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Coverage gap worth auditing in any SSR build: dependency-graph-scoped linting can silently miss files.

insights.claim: The plugin was originally forked from eslint-webpack-plugin and retains a familiar configuration surface, which is what makes webpack-to-Rspack migration cheap at the tooling layer.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: API-compatibility-by-fork is Rspack's core adoption strategy; it lowers switching costs away from webpack.
insights.quote: It was originally forked from eslint-webpack-plugin, so its configuration surface feels familiar to webpack users.
insights.locator: Functionally the plugin continues to run ESLint
